title: Our Days, Alas! Our Mortal Days
description: Our Days, Alas! Our Mortal Days in Tonic Solfa to CAITHNESS, doh is D: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 4 verses and a piano.
about: Isaac Watts wrote these words for his Hymns and Spiritual Songs (1707), Book II, composed on divine subjects, hymn 39, headed “The shortness and misery of life”.
Watts' hymns were printed without tunes and sung to any tune of their metre, Common Metre (8.6.8.6). This page sets the words to CAITHNESS; any other Common Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: Our days, a-las! our mor-tal days Are short and wret-ched too; "E-vil and few," the pa-triarch says, And well the pa-triarch knew.

lines: Our days, alas! our mortal days
'Tis but at best a narrow bound
And pains and sins run thro' the round
Well, if ye must be sad and few,
Run on, my days, in haste;
Moments of sin, and months of woe,
Let heavenly love prepare my soul,
And call her to the skies,
Where years of long salvation roll,

source: Isaac Watts, Hymns and Spiritual Songs (1707)
licence: Public domain: Isaac Watts died in 1748.
credits: Words by Isaac Watts (1674–1748), public domain; set to CAITHNESS by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
